steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our paper on a dynamic edge partition model for temporal graphs that can be trained with stochastic gradient MCMC. It should cover why graph modelling matters, why the EPM is attractive but hard to scale, what our new model does differently, and how the rest of the paper is organized.

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Graph-structured data analysis has been an active research area, because it has many applications in social network analysis, recommender system and knowledge graph embedding. In the last decade there have been many efforts to model graph-structured data, for example the stochastic block model (SBM), the latent feature relational model (LFRM) and the edge partition model (EPM). Out of these methods, the EPM has received a lot of attention because it has some appealing properties. (1) It adopts the gamma process prior, which automatically infers the appropriate number of latent communities. (2) Each vertex is represented by a gamma distributed positive memberships vector, which is highly interpretable and lets us extract an overlapping community structure from the network. (3) The EPM model enjoys full local conjugacy, and it admits an MCMC algorithm for posterior computation that is simple to implement, using data augmentation and a marginalization strategy. The EPM has also been extended to multi-relational graph learning, deep generative graph modelling, inductive matrix completion and dynamic network modelling.

The EPM and its extensions achieve competitive performance in a variety of applications, but inference in these models is done with MCMC methods, and these notoriously mix slowly and do not scale well to large datasets in practice. Real temporal graph-structured data, for example user-user interactions in social networks or user-item ratings in recommender systems, easily get to millions of vertices and edges. So it is highly desirable to have a scalable inference algorithm for the EPM and its extensions.

In this work we propose a new generative model that extends the gamma process edge partition model (GaP-EPM) to model temporal assortative graphs. Each vertex gets a positive memberships vector that is constructed using a Dirichlet prior specification, and this keeps the expressiveness and interpretability of the original EPM. The new model uses a Dirichlet Markov chain to capture how the memberships of the vertices evolve smoothly over time. Unlike the original EPM construction, the ideal number of latent communities is inferred adaptively using the hierarchical beta-gamma prior specification. We note that the edge partition model has already been extended to temporal networks by evolving the vertex memberships through a gamma Markov chain construction. But the gamma priors construction of the original GaP-EPM can disturb the model shrinkage effect, which results in overestimating the number of communities, as was shown in prior work. To deal with this, we build a new model using the hierarchical beta-gamma prior, which prevents overfitting. In particular, because of the unique construction of the Dirichlet Markov chain, we can adopt the recently advanced SG-MCMC algorithms for scalable and parallelizable inference in the proposed model. The rest of the paper is structured like this. First we review the relevant backgrounds. Then we present the new dynamic edge partition model and describe its Gibbs sampler and SG-MCMC algorithm. We show the accuracy and efficiency of our method on several real-world datasets. Finally we conclude the paper and discuss future research.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Analysis of graph-structured data has been an active research area because of its many applications in social network analysis [1], recommender systems [2,3,4] and knowledge graph embedding [5,6,7]. Over the last decade, many efforts have been devoted to modelling graph-structured data, such as the stochastic block model (SBM) [8], the latent feature relational model (LFRM) [9] and the edge partition model (EPM) [10]. Among these methods, the EPM has drawn much attention because of its appealing properties: (1) the gamma process prior is adopted to automatically infer the appropriate number of latent communities; (2) each vertex is represented by a gamma distributed positive memberships vector that is highly interpretable and allows us to extract an overlapping community structure from the given network; (3) the EPM enjoys full local conjugacy and admits a simple-to-implement MCMC algorithm for posterior computation using data augmentation and marginalization. The EPM has also been extended to multi-relational graph learning [11], deep generative graph modelling [12], inductive matrix completion [13,14], and dynamic network modelling [15,16,17,18]. While the EPM and its extensions achieve competitive performance in various applications, inference in these models is done via MCMC methods that notoriously mix slowly and scale poorly to large datasets in practice. Real temporal graph-structured data, such as user-user interactions in social networks or user-item ratings in recommender systems, easily run into millions of vertices and edges. Hence, it is highly desirable to develop a scalable inference algorithm for the EPM and its extensions.

In this work, we propose a novel generative model that extends the gamma process edge partition model (GaP-EPM) to temporal assortative graphs by endowing each vertex with a positive memberships vector, constructed using a Dirichlet prior specification, which retains the expressiveness and interpretability of the original EPM. Specifically, the new model uses a Dirichlet Markov chain to capture the smooth evolution of the vertices' memberships over time. Unlike in the original EPM construction, the ideal number of latent communities is inferred adaptively using the hierarchical beta-gamma prior specification [19]. Note that the edge partition model has been extended to temporal networks by evolving vertex memberships through a gamma Markov chain construction [16]. However, the gamma priors construction of the original GaP-EPM can disturb the model shrinkage effect and thus lead to overestimation of the number of communities, as shown in [20]. To counteract this, we build a novel model using the hierarchical beta-gamma prior to prevent overfitting. In particular, the unique construction of the Dirichlet Markov chain enables us to adopt the recently advanced SG-MCMC algorithms [21,22,23,24,25] for scalable and parallelizable inference in the proposed model. The remainder of the paper is structured as follows. We first review the relevant background. Then we present the novel dynamic edge partition model and describe its Gibbs sampler and SG-MCMC algorithm. We demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of our method on several real-world datasets. Finally, we conclude the paper and discuss future research.
